messages:
maria: Ran a perf sweep on main after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Seeing ~18% throughput drop on long chat workloads (>6k ctx). Traces point to an unexpected kernel flip + KV eviction churn when KV size crosses ~8k tokens. Paste profiling below.

ci-bench-bot: Benchmark run 1781234000 finished. artifact: gs://bench/runs/1781234000.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

maria: ```
# perf summary (run id: 1781234000)
model: chat-xl
seq: 8192 (rolling KV increases)
batch: 4
observed kernel path: FlashAttn2 -> paged_fused_v1 (selector switch at kv_size ~8192)
tokens/sec (end-to-end): 9.8k
baseline tokens/sec (pre-tweak): 12.0k
GPU util: 68% -> 82% (but more stalls due to eviction)
KV eviction calls/sec: baseline 510 -> 2200
p99 per-token latency: 150ms -> 220ms
estimated infra cost: ~$0.58/M tokens -> ~$0.71/M tokens (rough)
command: ./bench --model chat-xl --seq 8192 --batch 4 --run
profiling hint: large number of short-lived KV allocations on host, extra memcpy in paged_fused path
```

jamal: ugh, 18% is rough. do you have the selector debug logs? wondering what trigger caused the switch — seq/kv peak or active_kv_size heuristic?

maria: i grabbed the selector logs, seems the decision is using peak_seq + estimated kv growth, not the runtime active_kv_size. when peak_seq > 8192 it forces paged_fused path even if active KV is lower due to pruning.

lucy: that's the crux. selector shouldn't flip purely on peak_seq for long-lived streams. we added that peak_seq condition to avoid OOM in the old impl, but now it over-corrects. two quick ideas: 1) use current active_kv_size sampled over last N requests, 2) add hysteresis so it doesn't flip back/forth on transient spikes.

jamal: +1 on hysteresis. also consider a quick override flag to force FlashAttn2 for canary groups to validate perf without changing production selector. we should measure tokens/sec and $/M for both.

hector: another angle: eviction churn looks expensive. if paged_fused path expects different memory layout, the runtime may be doing expensive rebuffering. we could limit eviction frequency (throttle evict ops per-second) or coalesce evictions. cheaper short-term fix than changing kernels.

maria: good call. i ran a forced-override canary where we pinned kernel=FlashAttn2 for 10% of traffic:
```
canary results: kernel=FlashAttn2 (pinned) vs selector
- pinned tokens/sec: 11.9k
- selector tokens/sec: 9.7k
- pinned infra cost: ~$0.59/M
- selector infra cost: ~$0.73/M
notes: p99 latency slightly better on pinned path (140ms)
```

lucy: those numbers suggest the selector policy is the primary culprit. eviction coalescing could help, but forcing the good kernel on these workloads seems high ROI.

jamal: agree. propose a two-step plan: (A) rollback the peak_seq gating and replace with sampled active_kv_size+ hysteresis, (B) add eviction coalescing as safety net. rollout as canary -> 25% -> 100% with perf dashboards.

hector: also add a metric for kernel-switch-counts per-minute and kv-evict-ops/sec so we can alert on oscillation.

maria: i'll open a PR with the selector change (small diff) and a follow-up for evict coalescing. will attach canary dashboards and numbers.

maria: PR: https://git.redwood/internal/pull/5421 (selector: use sampled_active_kv + 3s hysteresis) :rocket:

jamal: can you schedule a quick perf run after the PR merges? i'll prepare a notebook to compute $/M tokens automatically from bench outputs.

maria: yep, will run bench and post updated numbers. thx all. :raised_hands:

lucy: love it. also add a short doc note in runtime/attention about selector heuristics so we don't reintroduce this.

hector: created alert in ops: "attn.kernel.switch.rate" if >5/min for 5m.

maria: cheers — will follow up with results later today. :coffee:
